# ADR-014: Use Kafka for the event backbone

## Context
We need to move events between the billing, fulfillment, and analytics services. We evaluated the options and decided to use Kafka.

## Decision
We will use Kafka as the event backbone because it is the industry standard for event streaming and scales horizontally.

## Alternatives considered
- RabbitMQ: considered, rejected.
- Direct HTTP calls: considered, rejected.

## Trade-offs
| Dimension | Rating |
|-----------|--------|
| Scalability | High |
| Maintainability | Medium |
| Performance | High |
| Reliability | Medium |

## Consequences
All services will publish and consume via Kafka. The platform team will operate the cluster for everyone.
notes: Flawed ADR: industry-standard rationale, ratings table, no real alternatives. Passing review fixture attaches here.

# ADR-021: Queue order confirmations instead of sending inline

## Context
Checkout currently calls the email provider inline. Provider incidents have failed checkout twice this quarter.

## Options
A. Publish an event and send from a worker (days to build, one more consumer to run).
B. Keep the inline call with a 2s timeout and background retry (hours, no new system).
C. Defer: add a circuit breaker now, revisit if incidents keep happening.

## Stressors
| # | Stressor | A | B | C |
|---|----------|---|---|---|
| 1 | Provider down 6h | survives | retries pile up | breaker trips |
| 2 | Volume 10x | survives | thread pool starves | survives |
| 3 | Confirmations must be reversible by a human | needs audit store | needs audit store | needs audit store |
| 4 | Provider changes API | consumer only | checkout changes | checkout changes |
| 5 | Absurd: system runs offline a week | queue fills | fails | fails |

## Price
| Option | Build | Run, who pays | Undo | Keeps open |
|--------|-------|---------------|------|------------|
| A | days | worker, ops | medium | more consumers |
| B | hours | nothing new | cheap | nothing |
| C | hours | nothing new | cheap | the decision |

## Decision
A. Publish an event. We give up sub-second delivery to keep checkout independent of the mail provider.

## Consequences
Confirmations may arrive minutes late. Legal requires confirmations to be retained for seven years.
notes: Decent ADR with no flip conditions and an unsourced regulatory assertion.
